post.title: Why You Should Never Shop Hungry #shorts
post.description: Which snack always sneaks into your basket? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend who shops starving. Otto went in for milk and came out with six snacks. In 'Predicting Hunger: The Effects of Appetite and Delay on Choice' (Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 1998), Daniel Read and Barbara van Leeuwen asked 200 employees in Amsterdam to choose a snack they would get a week later. People who chose while hungry picked unhealthy snacks more often than people who chose after lunch, whether or not they would be hungry when the snack arrived. How you feel right now leaks into choices for future you. It's called the hot-cold empathy gap. Eat first, then shop. #psychology #shorts #hotcoldempathygap #decisions #overthinking

lines.say: In nineteen ninety-eight, two hundred workers picked a snack for next week.

lines.text: Hungry pickers chose more JUNK, however full they'd be later.
Think of the 'healthy week' you planned after DINNER. Yeah, that one.
